title: Full Business English Shadowing Practice | Speak English Fluently at Work

segments.text: Hello everyone and welcome back to business English for success.
segments.ipa: /həˈloʊ ˈɛvriˌwʌn ənd ˈwɛlkəm bæk tu ˈbɪznəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ fɔr səkˈsɛs/

segments.text: If you've been learning business English for a while, you probably already understand a lot of the English you hear at work.
segments.ipa: /ɪf juv bɪn ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈbɪznəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ fɔr ə waɪl ju ˈprɑbəˌbli ɔlˈrɛdi ˌʌndərˈstænd ə lɑt ʌv ðə ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ju hir æt wɝk/

segments.text: But knowing what to say is one thing.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈnoʊɪŋ wʌt tu seɪ ɪz wʌn θɪŋ/

segments.text: Being able to say it naturally when someone is actually waiting for your answer is another.
segments.ipa: /ˈbiɪŋ ˈeɪbəl tu seɪ ɪt ˈnætʃərəli wɛn ˈsʌmˌwʌn ɪz ˈækˌtʃuəli ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr jɔr ˈænsər ɪz əˈnʌðər/

segments.text: And that's what we're going to practice today.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðæts wʌt wir ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu ˈpræktəs təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: This is a full business English shadowing session built around situations you actually deal with at work.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə fʊl ˈbɪznəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈʃædoʊɪŋ ˈsɛʃən bɪlt ərˈaʊnd ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃənz ju ˈækˌtʃuəli dil wɪð æt wɝk/

segments.text: We'll start with everyday conversations, checking something with a colleague, asking for help, following up,
segments.ipa: /wil stɑrt wɪð ˈɛvriˈdeɪ ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz ˈtʃɛkɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ wɪð ə ˈkɑliɡ ˈæskɪŋ fɔr hɛlp ˈfɑloʊɪŋ ʌp/

segments.text: and giving useful updates.
segments.ipa: /ənd ˈɡɪvɪŋ ˈjusfəl əpˈdeɪts/

segments.text: Then we'll move into conversations with your manager, especially when you need to talk about progress,
segments.ipa: /ðɛn wil muv ˈɪntu ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz wɪð jɔr ˈmænədʒər əˈspɛʃli wɛn ju nid tu tɔk əˈbaʊt ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: priorities, or a deadline you're not ready to promise yet.
segments.ipa: /praɪˈɔrətiz ɔr ə ˈdɛdˌlaɪn jʊr nɑt ˈrɛdi tu ˈprɑməs jɛt/

segments.text: And we'll take you through a business meeting from beginning to end, from opening the meeting and giving updates to joining the discussion,
segments.ipa: /ənd wil teɪk ju θru ə ˈbɪznəs ˈmitɪŋ frʌm bɪˈɡɪnɪŋ tu ɛnd frʌm ˈoʊpənɪŋ ðə ˈmitɪŋ ənd ˈɡɪvɪŋ əpˈdeɪts tu ˈdʒɔɪnɪŋ ðə dɪˈskʌʃən/

segments.text: disagreeing professionally, working toward a decision, and closing with clear next steps.
segments.ipa: /dɪsəˈɡriɪŋ prəˈfɛʃənəli ˈwɝkɪŋ təˈwɔrd ə dɪˈsɪʒən ənd ˈkloʊzɪŋ wɪð klɪr nɛkst stɛps/

segments.text: So, you're not practicing a few isolated phrases.
segments.ipa: /soʊ jʊr nɑt ˈpræktəsɪŋ ə fju ˈaɪsəˌleɪtəd ˈfreɪzəz/

segments.text: You're practicing the English you need as the conversation actually develops.
segments.ipa: /jʊr ˈpræktəsɪŋ ðə ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ju nid æz ðə ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən ˈækˌtʃuəli dɪˈvɛləps/

segments.text: And we're going to spend most of our time practicing, not explaining.
segments.ipa: /ənd wir ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu spɛnd moʊst ʌv ˈaʊər taɪm ˈpræktəsɪŋ nɑt ɪkˈspleɪnɪŋ/

segments.text: We'll give you just enough context to know when you might use each response.
segments.ipa: /wil ɡɪv ju dʒʌst ɪˈnʌf ˈkɑntɛkst tu noʊ wɛn ju maɪt jus itʃ rɪˈspɑns/

segments.text: You'll hear each response twice.
segments.ipa: /jul hir itʃ rɪˈspɑns twaɪs/

segments.text: Listen carefully the first time.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən ˈkɛrfəli ðə fɝst taɪm/

segments.text: The second time, say it with us and try to follow the rhythm of the whole response.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈsɛkənd taɪm seɪ ɪt wɪð ʌs ənd traɪ tu ˈfɑloʊ ðə ˈrɪðəm ʌv ðə hoʊl rɪˈspɑns/

segments.text: Don't worry about memorizing every word.
segments.ipa: /doʊnt ˈwɝi əˈbaʊt ˈmɛmərˌaɪzɪŋ ˈɛvəri wɝd/

segments.text: If you're somewhere you can't speak out loud, just listen.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jʊr ˈsʌmˌwɛr ju kænt spik aʊt laʊd dʒʌst ˈlɪsən/

segments.text: You can always come back and practice later.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈɔlˌweɪz kʌm bæk ənd ˈpræktəs ˈleɪtər/

segments.text: But whenever you can, say the responses with us.
segments.ipa: /bʌt wɛˈnɛvər ju kæn seɪ ðə rɪˈspɑnsɪz wɪð ʌs/

segments.text: The more often you actually use this English, the easier it becomes to reach for it when you need it at work.
segments.ipa: /ðə mɔr ˈɔfən ju ˈækˌtʃuəli jus ðɪs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ðə ˈiziər ɪt bɪˈkʌmz tu ritʃ fɔr ɪt wɛn ju nid ɪt æt wɝk/

segments.text: All right, let's get started with the English you probably use most often, everyday conversations at work.
segments.ipa: /ɔl raɪt lɛts ɡɛt ˈstɑrtɪd wɪð ðə ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ju ˈprɑbəˌbli jus moʊst ˈɔfən ˈɛvriˈdeɪ ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz æt wɝk/

segments.text: Let's start with the kind of English you probably use all the time at work.

segments.text: Checking something with a colleague, asking for help, giving an update, or following up on something you need.
segments.ipa: /ˈtʃɛkɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ wɪð ə ˈkɑliɡ ˈæskɪŋ fɔr hɛlp ˈɡɪvɪŋ æn əpˈdeɪt ɔr ˈfɑloʊɪŋ ʌp ɑn ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju nid/

segments.text: James, could you bring us up to speed on where things stand? Sure.
segments.ipa: /dʒeɪmz kʊd ju brɪŋ ʌs ʌp tu spid ɑn wɛr θɪŋz stænd ʃʊr/

segments.text: We've completed most of the testing and the results look good so far.
segments.ipa: /wiv kəmˈplitəd moʊst ʌv ðə ˈtɛstɪŋ ənd ðə rɪˈzʌlts lʊk ɡʊd soʊ fɑr/

segments.text: The main issue is that we're still waiting for the supplier to confirm when the final component will arrive.
segments.ipa: /ðə meɪn ˈɪʃu ɪz ðæt wir stɪl ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr ðə səˈplaɪər tu kənˈfɝm wɛn ðə ˈfaɪnəl kəmˈpoʊnənt wɪl ərˈaɪv/

segments.text: Do we know when they're likely to confirm that?
segments.ipa: /du wi noʊ wɛn ðɛr ˈlaɪkli tu kənˈfɝm ðæt/

segments.text: They've said they'll come back to us this afternoon.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪv sɛd ðeɪl kʌm bæk tu ʌs ðɪs ˌæftərˈnun/

segments.text: If the component arrives by Tuesday, we should still be able to keep the current launch date.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ðə kəmˈpoʊnənt ərˈaɪvz baɪ ˈtuzdi wi ʃʊd stɪl bi ˈeɪbəl tu kip ðə ˈkɝənt lɔntʃ deɪt/

segments.text: And if it doesn't?
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf ɪt ˈdʌzənt/

segments.text: Then Friday becomes difficult.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ˈfraɪdi bɪˈkʌmz ˈdɪfəkəlt/

segments.text: We'd probably need either to delay the launch or release without that part of the product.
segments.ipa: /wid ˈprɑbəˌbli nid ˈiðər tu dɪˈleɪ ðə lɔntʃ ɔr riˈlis wɪˈθaʊt ðæt pɑrt ʌv ðə ˈprɑdəkt/

segments.text: My feeling is that we shouldn't delay the whole launch because of one component.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈfilɪŋ ɪz ðæt wi ˈʃʊdənt dɪˈleɪ ðə hoʊl lɔntʃ bɪˈkɔz ʌv wʌn kəmˈpoʊnənt/

segments.text: If everything else is ready, I'd rather reduce the scope of the first release and add the remaining feature later.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ ɛls ɪz ˈrɛdi aɪd ˈræðər rəˈdus ðə skoʊp ʌv ðə fɝst riˈlis ənd æd ðə rɪˈmeɪnɪŋ ˈfitʃər ˈleɪtər/

segments.text: I see your point, but I'm slightly concerned about how the client will react.
segments.ipa: /aɪ si jɔr pɔɪnt bʌt aɪm ˈslaɪtli kənˈsɝnd əˈbaʊt haʊ ðə ˈklaɪənt wɪl riˈækt/

segments.text: They've been expecting the full release on Friday.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪv bɪn ɪkˈspɛktɪŋ ðə fʊl riˈlis ɑn ˈfraɪdi/

segments.text: That's true, but I think they'll be more comfortable with a smaller release that works properly than a full release we aren't confident in.
segments.ipa: /ðæts tru bʌt aɪ θɪŋk ðeɪl bi mɔr ˈkʌmfərtəbəl wɪð ə ˈsmɔlər riˈlis ðæt wɝks ˈprɑpərli ðæn ə fʊl riˈlis wi ˈɑrənt ˈkɑnfədənt ɪn/

segments.text: Could we speak to them before we decide?
segments.ipa: /kʊd wi spik tu ðɛm bɪˈfɔr wi ˌdɪˈsaɪd/

segments.text: We could explain the situation and see whether they'd prefer a smaller release on Friday or the complete version a few days later.
segments.ipa: /wi kʊd ɪkˈspleɪn ðə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən ənd si ˈwɛðər ðeɪd prəˈfɝ ə ˈsmɔlər riˈlis ɑn ˈfraɪdi ɔr ðə kəmˈplit ˈvɝʒən ə fju deɪz ˈleɪtər/

segments.text: I think that's probably the best way forward.
segments.ipa: /aɪ θɪŋk ðæts ˈprɑbəˌbli ðə bɛst weɪ ˈfɔrwərd/

segments.text: There's one other thing we need to consider though.
segments.ipa: /ðɛrz wʌn ˈʌðər θɪŋ wi nid tu kənˈsɪdər ðoʊ/

segments.text: If we delay, do we know what impact that would have on the team next week? Not yet.
segments.ipa: /ɪf wi dɪˈleɪ du wi noʊ wʌt ˌɪmˈpækt ðæt wʊd hæv ɑn ðə tim nɛkst wik nɑt jɛt/

segments.text: I'd need to check with the project leads.
segments.ipa: /aɪd nid tu tʃɛk wɪð ðə ˈprɑdʒɛkt lidz/

segments.text: Several people are due to move on to other work after Friday.
segments.ipa: /ˈsɛvrəl ˈpipəl ɑr du tu muv ɑn tu ˈʌðər wɝk ˈæftər ˈfraɪdi/

segments.text: Okay, in that case, I don't think we have enough information to make the final decision right now.
segments.ipa: /ˌoʊˈkeɪ ɪn ðæt keɪs aɪ doʊnt θɪŋk wi hæv ɪˈnʌf ˌɪnfərˈmeɪʃən tu meɪk ðə ˈfaɪnəl dɪˈsɪʒən raɪt naʊ/

segments.text: Let's do two things.
segments.ipa: /lɛts du tu θɪŋz/

segments.text: I'll speak to the client this afternoon and find out which option they would prefer.
segments.ipa: /aɪl spik tu ðə ˈklaɪənt ðɪs ˌæftərˈnun ənd faɪnd aʊt wɪtʃ ˈɑpʃən ðeɪ wʊd prəˈfɝ/

segments.text: James, could you check with the project leads and confirm what a delay would mean for the team?
segments.ipa: /dʒeɪmz kʊd ju tʃɛk wɪð ðə ˈprɑdʒɛkt lidz ənd kənˈfɝm wʌt ə dɪˈleɪ wʊd min fɔr ðə tim/

segments.text: Yes, I'll do that. Great.
segments.ipa: /jɛs aɪl du ðæt ɡreɪt/

segments.text: Let's aim to have both answers by the end of today.
segments.ipa: /lɛts eɪm tu hæv boʊθ ˈænsərz baɪ ðə ɛnd ʌv təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Once we have them, we can make the final call tomorrow morning.
segments.ipa: /wʌns wi hæv ðɛm wi kæn meɪk ðə ˈfaɪnəl kɔl təˈmɑˌroʊ ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

segments.text: Is there anything else we need to cover?
segments.ipa: /ɪz ðɛr ˈɛniˌθɪŋ ɛls wi nid tu ˈkʌvər/

segments.text: Nothing for me.
segments.ipa: /ˈnʌθɪŋ fɔr mi/

segments.text: All right, let's leave it there. Thanks, everyone.
segments.ipa: /ɔl raɪt lɛts liv ɪt ðɛr θæŋks ˈɛvriˌwʌn/

segments.text: I'll send a quick summary of the next steps after the meeting.
segments.ipa: /aɪl sɛnd ə kwɪk ˈsʌməri ʌv ðə nɛkst stɛps ˈæftər ðə ˈmitɪŋ/

segments.text: And that brings us to the end of today's business English shadowing practice.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðæt brɪŋz ʌs tu ðə ɛnd ʌv təˈdeɪz ˈbɪznəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈʃædoʊɪŋ ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: You've practiced a lot of real workplace English today, from everyday conversations and talking with your manager to working through a business meeting from beginning to end.
segments.ipa: /juv ˈpræktəst ə lɑt ʌv ril ˈwɝkˌpleɪs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ təˈdeɪ frʌm ˈɛvriˈdeɪ ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz ənd ˈtɔkɪŋ wɪð jɔr ˈmænədʒər tu ˈwɝkɪŋ θru ə ˈbɪznəs ˈmitɪŋ frʌm bɪˈɡɪnɪŋ tu ɛnd/

segments.text: If some of these responses still feel difficult, come back and practice them again.
segments.ipa: /ɪf sʌm ʌv ðiz rɪˈspɑnsɪz stɪl fil ˈdɪfəkəlt kʌm bæk ənd ˈpræktəs ðɛm əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: The more often you actually say this English yourself, the easier it becomes to use when you need it at work.
segments.ipa: /ðə mɔr ˈɔfən ju ˈækˌtʃuəli seɪ ðɪs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ jərˈsɛlf ðə ˈiziər ɪt bɪˈkʌmz tu jus wɛn ju nid ɪt æt wɝk/

segments.text: And in our next shadowing session, we'll practice conversations with clients and other teams,
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪn ˈaʊər nɛkst ˈʃædoʊɪŋ ˈsɛʃən wil ˈpræktəs ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz wɪð ˈklaɪənts ənd ˈʌðər timz/

segments.text: along with some of those more difficult situations at work.
segments.ipa: /əˈlɔŋ wɪð sʌm ʌv ðoʊz mɔr ˈdɪfəkəlt ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃənz æt wɝk/

segments.text: If there's a workplace situation you'd like to practice with us, let us know in the comments.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ðɛrz ə ˈwɝkˌpleɪs ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən jud laɪk tu ˈpræktəs wɪð ʌs lɛt ʌs noʊ ɪn ðə ˈkɑmɛnts/

segments.text: Thanks for practicing with us today, and we'll see you in the next business English for success lesson.
segments.ipa: /θæŋks fɔr ˈpræktəsɪŋ wɪð ʌs təˈdeɪ ənd wil si ju ɪn ðə nɛkst ˈbɪznəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ fɔr səkˈsɛs ˈlɛsən/
